items.desc: Health workers have begun door-to-door testing and treatment as two to five people test positive each day in the rural municipality.

items.title: China’s Xi expected to press Trump to halt Taiwan arms sales under 1982 agreement, sources say
items.desc: China regularly describes the issue of Taiwan, which Beijing views ‌as its own territory, as its most sensitive and important diplomatic issue and has repeatedly called for arms sales to stop.

items.title: Remittances built Nepal’s economy for decades. It’s time for the next step
items.desc: Upgrading data-sharing and recruitment systems can bridge the gap between Nepali workers and foreign employers, fostering a sustainable win-win economic model.

items.title: Pedestrian overpass takes shape in Babarmahal
items.desc: The footbridge is being built along the busy Maitighar–New Baneshwar section to make road crossings safer for pedestrians.

items.desc: Nepal’s prime minister says syndicates and intermediaries have harmed workers and calls for direct talks between the two countries’ labour ministers.

items.title: Nepal-Japan festival to mark 70 years of diplomatic ties
items.desc: The November 22 event in Kathmandu will feature Japanese band Godiego, Nepali artists and cultural, tourism and commercial activities.

items.title: Bus driver who set vehicle on fire was absconding after Balaju crash, police say
items.desc: The driver who died of burns was allegedly using driving licences issued in other people’s names.

items.title: They crossed borders and jungles for America. Many returned afraid to speak
items.desc: In just a year, hundreds of Nepalis have been deported after paying millions to reach the US through the so-called ‘donkey route’. Why are so few willing to report those who sent them?

items.title: Balendra Shah is breaking with the tradition of the airport farewell
items.desc: The prime minister will leave for New York without a guard of honour, red carpet or the customary gathering of ministers and foreign diplomats.

items.title: The dangerous hunt for yarsagumba is no longer paying off for Karnali’s collectors
items.desc: Falling prices, declining production and the absence of Chinese buyers are squeezing communities that have long depended on the prized fungus.

items.title: Butwal-Gorusinge road upgrade is just 28 percent complete with a year left
items.desc: Shortages of soil and riverbed materials, delays in relocating utility poles and a sharp drop in the workforce are slowing the Rs13.55-billion project to build a climate-resilient four-lane highway.

items.title: US to open two new military bases in Greenland
items.desc: The agreement would expand the US military presence in Greenland as Washington, Copenhagen and Nuuk seek to strengthen Arctic security amid President Donald Trump’s push for greater US control of the territory.

items.title: Foreign Minister Khanal begins bilateral meetings in New York
items.desc: Foreign leaders and senior officials voice solidarity over Nepal’s climate justice position and flood recovery on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

items.desc: Nepal’s prime minister is set to address the General Assembly on climate justice, the Bhotekoshi floods and the concerns of mountain countries.

items.title: Mental wellbeing: What happens when a label becomes your identity?
items.desc: Calling someone ‘weak’, ‘shy’ or ‘smart’ may seem like a simple description. But repeated labels can shape how people understand themselves.

items.title: Rain is coming again. This time, Nepal must be prepared
items.desc: Sound preparation and competent governance can reduce the damage of forecasted heavy rain.

items.title: What Babita Paswan’s ordeal says about the state of Nepal’s weakest citizens
items.desc: Having a right in law and being able to exercise that right in life are not the same thing.

items.title: What the Bhotekoshi flood revealed about Nepal’s health system
items.desc: The emergency phase of the flood has largely been contained, but the most demanding work still lies ahead.

items.title: New hybrid maize variety ‘Saugat’ promises relief for farmers facing extreme weather
items.desc: The variety is on the verge of official certification and release after nearly 11 years of rigorous multi-stage field trials and continuous testing.

items.title: The nurse who wanted to heal Rasuwa
items.desc: Pratima Tamang Lama was a nurse, community worker, and ambitious local leader who dreamed of becoming Nepal’s health minister. The Bhotekoshi flood cut those dreams short.

items.title: Recurring tech failures rattle Nepal’s stock market
items.desc: Repeated breakdowns at Nepse, broker firms, data centres and trading systems are eroding investor confidence and raising concerns over the security of more than Rs4.5 trillion in assets.

items.title: Nepal’s 74-year-old Law Commission remains sidelined in lawmaking
items.desc: The body was created to research, draft and review laws, but most of its bills never reach Parliament, while ministries continue to make legislation that often becomes contentious.

items.title: Nepal unlikely to hold donor conference for reconstruction
items.desc: The government plans to seek funds through bilateral negotiations with major donors.

items.title: Bhat-Bhateni rebuilds 10 stores damaged during Gen Z uprising
items.desc: Despite the destruction and damage to its stores on September 9, 2025, the supermarket chain continued paying over 10,000 employees and began clearing debris within a week.

items.title: Supreme Court orders police not to routinely handcuff people arrested for investigation
items.desc: Handcuffs may be used only after an objective assessment finds a risk of escape, resistance or harm to the detainee or others, the court says.

items.title: Government weighs scrapping VAT on electricity
items.desc: The tax was introduced in the current budget, with a five percent rate for household users and 13 percent for others, but the government is now considering reversing the move.
